title: Bonnabelle Zabelle
text:
Hey there, hi there, ho there!
I am a data scientist with a background in Astrophysics research, I have been working with big data for the past 4 years. I got my B.S. in Astrophysics from the University of Minnesota in 2021. I then took a gap year working as a researcher under Prof. Claudia Scarlata. This work led me to apply to graduate school, where I ended up attending the University of Minnesota for a Masters of Science in Astrophysics, which I received at the beginning of 2025. Much of my research has been in extragalactic evolution, with an emphasis on studying star-formation rates in galaxies. Due to my affiliation with the Euclid Space Telescope I also dedicated much of my time in my masters program to working with the Euclid data pipeline, working in structure (SQL) and unstructured (DBview) databases. This work led to multiple contributions to the Euclid collaboration, mostly in the form of data validation and the creation of python-based data pipelines that enabled scientists to access Euclid data before their scheduled releases.
My education and research have led me to develop a wide array of tools well befitting that of a data scientist, from modern AI and machine learning to classics like MCMC and regression. Astrophysics has been the birthplace of many modern statistical and computational techniques, and has uniquely prepared me to embrace the ever-changing landscape of data science.
